# Autonomous Loops

Curated by Skill Harbor: patterns, architectures and reference implementations for running Claude Code autonomously in loops, from the simplest to the most sophisticated. The spectrum covers sequential pipelines of non-interactive claude -p calls for scripted daily work; the NanoClaw REPL for interactive persistent sessions; infinite agentic loops for parallel content generation and spec-driven work; continuous PR loops for multi-day iterative projects with CI gates; the de-sloppify cleanup pass after any implementer step; and Ralphinho-style RFC-driven multi-agent DAG orchestration with a merge queue for large features. Covers choosing the right loop architecture for the problem, context persistence across iterations, parallel agents with merge coordination, and quality gates with cleanup passes. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: retained for compatibility only, the canonical skill is now continuous-agent-loop, so prefer that for new work; autonomous loops multiply token spend and need stop conditions plus human oversight. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
